title: Idle capacity hedge and escalation playbook (PRD - WIP)
summary: A pragmatic playbook for reserving and consuming short-term idle GPU capacity to smooth customer-facing bursts while preserving tenant isolation and predictable SLAs. Focus: policy grammar + escalation triggers + operator runbook + quick rollout steps.
background: We see repeated short spikes from a subset of Dedicated customers (microbursts ~10-30s and sustained surges 3-20 min). Existing reserved capacity + warm pools are expensive to keep universally. This doc sketches a hedging layer that temporarily leverages idle or preemptible capacity within a safe economic and isolation envelope, with automatic escalation and clear operator controls.
problem_statement: How can Redwood provide cost-efficient burst capacity to Dedicated tenants without increasing noisy-neighbor risk or breaking latency SLOs for committed capacity customers? We need a policy that: 1) surfaces idle capacity reliably, 2) decides whether to lend that capacity to a bursting tenant, 3) guarantees rollback and graceful degradation, 4) records auditable chargebacks and fallbacks.
non_goals: This playbook does NOT replace long-term reserved capacity commitments, does NOT attempt to unify hosted and dedicated billing models, and does NOT cover on-prem private deployments (though concepts may be portable).
requirements: R1: Borrow window — short-lived borrowings (30s–15min) with per-tenant max concurrency and token accounting
R2: Isolation fences — borrowed capacity must be revocable within 2s on preemption signal and fall back to a lower-fidelity model or queued requests
R3: Cost guardrails — automatic cost cap per tenant per billing period with opt-in/opt-out
R4: Telemetry contract — traceable lifecycle for each borrow (candidate node, start/end timestamps, preemption reason, redirect target), surfaced in Console
R5: Escalation policy — automated rollback paths and human operator escalation if eviction rate > 0.5% for 10m
R6: Safety budget — a global idle-capacity budget per region that never exceeds X% of total Dedicated GPUs (configurable), default 12%
R7: SLA preservation — committed tenants' latency SLOs take precedence; hedging should not increase their p99 by more than configured delta
design_overview: Three-layer system: discovery, allocation, and control. Discovery finds idle candidates via a 'quietness' score (recent CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hotness, memory residency). Allocation chooses which tenant gets which node and for how long using a lightweight auction (priority + bid credit + thermal fit). Control enforces revocation, preemption, and chargeback.
policy_primitives: Quietness score (0-100): rolling 2m aggregation of gpu_util, queue_depth, active_kvcache_fraction
Borrow token: 1 token == ephemeral slot for N concurrent requests (configurable per model size)
Headroom reserve: min X% of a node pinned for committed tenants (node-level)
Eviction signal: 2-tier signal: SOFT (start draining new borrowed requests) / HARD (immediate kill of borrowed workloads)
Cost-credit ledger: per-tenant borrowing balance; integrates with billing to create line-item usage
escalation_and_fallbacks: Default automated flow: if preemption triggered for borrowed slot, in-order fallbacks: 1) transparent model downgrade to a pinned lower-fidelity variant, 2) route to tenant's reserved pool if available, 3) queue with exponential backoff and client 429 guidance. If eviction rate crosses threshold or headroom falls below reserve for committed tenants, system immediately suspends new borrows and opens an incident (SEV-lite) with on-call.
operator_runbook: 2) Console: open dedicated/hedge dashboard, filter by region and tenant
3) Check simulate-mode flag: if ON, toggles are logged but not enforced
4) If true negative impact on committed tenants observed (p99 increase > configured delta), toggle hedging to OFF for that region and start throttling borrows by 50%
5) Post-incident: run capacity-scan and label nodes that repeatedly flip between idle and hot — candidates for lifecycle policy or reprovisioning
6) Create CS ticket for affected tenants with transparent explanation and optional one-time bill credit (per policy)
metrics_and_slo: borrow_accept_rate (by tenant): percentage of borrow requests accepted
committed_p99_delta: observed p99 delta for committed tenants compared to baseline
cost_per_borrow_token: direct marginal cost estimate exported to billing
idle_utilization_fraction: fraction of idle budget actually used
rollout_plan: Phase 0: simulation only (2 weeks) — run scale-sim on real traces (refer linked notebook). Phase 1: beta with 5 non-critical customers + internal services (4 weeks) — opt-in only. Phase 2: broader opt-in for high-volume tenants with default conservative caps (8 weeks). Phase 3: region-wide enable with automated throttling and console controls. Each phase gated by measured committed_p99_delta < 2x delta_budget and borrow_preemption_rate < 0.2%.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Simulation shows net cost-savings > 8% for participants without SLO breaches
AC2: No committed-customer latency regression outside delta_budget during beta
AC3: Console shows per-tenant borrow audit trail and bill preview
AC4: On-call runbook validated in a canary incident
security_and_compliance_considerations: Borrowed workloads may execute on nodes that recently served other tenants. Ensure memory/KV eviction clears, ephemeral filesystem namespaces enforced, and audit logs contain tenant ids. For regulated tenants (HIPAA, SOC2 with stricter isolation), hedging defaults to OFF unless explicit approval and HSM key-handling constraints satisfied.
open_questions: Q1: Default global idle budget percentage — 12% is a starting point; does infra want region-specific flavors?
Q2: Billing model — immediate per-token chargeback vs periodic amortized credit?
Q3: Client API UX — should we return a borrow metadata header on responses? If so, what fields?
Q4: Thermal/energy constraints for on-prem customers — can we include energy-aware scoring?
Q5: Can we leverage preemptible spot capacity from cloud providers as part of the idle pool?
next_steps: 1) Gating PR to scale-sim repo to run 30-day production traces; 2) Instrument quietness score in telemetry pipeline; 3) Draft billing line-item and legal checklist for opt-in; 4) Prototype operator toggles in Console; 5) Book a cross-team review (infra, SRE, billing, CS) in next product sync.
notes_to_reviewers: This is a working playbook — aim is to capture operational boundaries, not final knobs. Key asks: infra (feasibility of 2s revoke), SRE (telemetry feasibility), billing (line-item design), CS (customer opt-in language).
